title: Local identity, sessions, authorization matrix, custody
mode: prototype-first (user directive D12): working authn/authz/custody proven hands-on over live PG + live HTTP; full custody state machine, matrix battery, VER batch and recovery flows deferred to wave 2
handover_note: Took over a dead worker's ~90%-complete uncommitted WIP. Read the full WIP first; the 3 QA failures in the inherited .omo/evidence/task-4-manual-qa.log were ALL driver-side defects of the lost driver, NOT code defects - the security logic shipped as-is, untouched (no security weakening).
defect_root_causes: owner GET notebook 200 + owner note-draft 200 (inherited failures a/b): the lost driver re-sent a REVOKED token after the owner re-login (its stale cookie resolved to None -> correct 401 'authentication required'). The rebuilt driver rides the TestClient cookie jar (the same flow the unit tests prove) and both checks now PASS with the code unchanged.

login rate limit 429 after four 401s (inherited failure c): the lost driver probed the rate limit with an email whose limiter key already held one attempt (the disabled-owner login check ran earlier on the same login:<ip>:<email> key). SlidingWindowLimiter(login_max_attempts=5) allows exactly five attempts in the 15-minute window and returns the uniform 429 on the sixth - the configured behavior. The rebuilt driver probes with a fresh account: statuses=[401,401,401,401,401,429] PASS.

runtime_deviations: PG runtime: the T3 digest-pinned PG18 rootfs scratch was wiped from /tmp by the host reboot, so the QA cluster runs the host PostgreSQL 17 server + pgvector 0.8.2 directly (scratch /tmp/opencode/fnd04-scratch, port 29518). The only PG18-specific element in the DDL is the uuidv7() PK default, emulated for the scratch cluster by a 4-line SQL shim (48-bit unix-ms timestamp | version 7 | variant 10 | rand) - scratch-only, never committed. Baseline migration applies on PG17 in ~110ms and the downgrade/upgrade symmetry was proven in T3 on PG18.

register-limiter budget: the configured default (3 registrations / IP / hour, uniform 429) is consumed by owner+viewer+newowner, so the rate-limit PROBE account is seeded via SQL with a real argon2id hash (its login key is what the check exercises). This is the limiter working as configured, not a gap.

CSRF middleware intercepts every unsafe /api/v1 request carrying a live session cookie (including POST /login) - the disabled-owner login probe runs with an empty cookie jar to isolate the authn outcome; the probe account's key is fresh so the 429 threshold is demonstrated exactly.
